ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
On November 12th, 13th, and 14th, our school will hold a sports meet. Students are actively preparing for this event during physical education classes and extracurricular activities. One of the team events is a 50-meter face-to-face relay race. Suppose during a training session, Student A starts from rest and accelerates to $v=8\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ in $t=2s$, then maintains this speed to pass the baton to Student B. If the acceleration phase is considered as uniformly accelerated linear motion.

1. What is the acceleration of student A during the acceleration phase?
2. What is the displacement of student A during the acceleration phase?
3. How much time did Student A take to complete this relay?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: On November 12th, 13th, and 14th, our school will hold a sports meet. Students are actively preparing for this event during physical education classes and extracurricular activities. One of the team events is a 50-meter face-to-face relay race. Suppose during a training session, Student A starts from rest and accelerates to $v=8\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ in $t=2s$, then maintains this speed to pass the baton to Student B. If the acceleration phase is considered as uniformly accelerated linear motion. 1. What is the acceleration of student A during the acceleration phase? 2. What is the displacement of student A during the acceleration phase? 3. How much time did Student A take to complete this relay?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: From the problem text: Student A starts from rest, so the initial speed is u = 0. Student A reaches v = 8 m/s in t = 2 s, and the acceleration phase is uniformly accelerated linear motion. The full relay distance for Student A is taken as 50 m, after which the baton is passed. 1. Acceleration during the acceleration phase: a = (v - u) / t = (8 - 0) / 2 = 4 m/s^2. 2. Displacement during the acceleration phase: s1 = ut + (1/2)at^2 = 0 × 2 + (1/2) × 4 × 2^2 = 8 m. 3. Total time to complete the 50 m relay: After accelerating, Student A has already covered 8 m, so the remaining distance is 50 - 8 = 42 m. At the constant speed 8 m/s, the time for the remaining distance is t2 = 42 / 8 = 5.25 s. Adding the acceleration time gives total time t_total = 2 + 5.25 = 7.25 s.
